Example 2: `isValidCreditCard('49927398717')` should return `false`.

title: Filter Inventory by Price Range
spec:
Write a function that filters an array of product objects based on a minimum and maximum price. Each product object has 'name' (string) and 'price' (number) properties. The function should return a new array containing only products within the specified price range (inclusive). Use the function `filterByPriceRange(products, minPrice, maxPrice)`.

Example: `filterByPriceRange([{name: 'A', price: 10}, {name: 'B', price: 25}], 15, 30)` should return `[{name: 'B', price: 25}]`.
Example: `filterByPriceRange([{name: 'C', price: 5}, {name: 'D', price: 100}], 0, 10)` should return `[{name: 'C', price: 5}]`.

title: Check if String is Palindrome
spec:
Implement a function that determines if a given string is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards), ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters. The function should take a string and return a boolean. Use the function `isPalindrome(str)`.

Example: `isPalindrome('Racecar')` should return `true`.
Example: `isPalindrome('Hello, world!')` should return `false`.

title: Simulate Basic User Login
spec:
Write a function that simulates a basic user login check. It should take a username and password (strings) and a `users` object (mapping usernames to passwords). It returns `true` if credentials match, `false` otherwise. Use the function `login(username, password, users)`.

Example: `login('user1', 'pass1', {user1: 'pass1', user2: 'pass2'})` should return `true`.
Example: `login('user1', 'wrong', {user1: 'pass1'})` should return `false`.

title: Calculate Rectangle Perimeter
spec:
Create a function that calculates the perimeter of a rectangle given its width and height. The function should accept two numbers and return a single number. Use the function `calculateRectanglePerimeter(width, height)`.

Example: `calculateRectanglePerimeter(5, 10)` should return `30`.
Example: `calculateRectanglePerimeter(2.5, 3)` should return `11`.

title: Count Inventory Items by Category
spec:
Write a function that takes an array of item objects (each with a 'name' and 'category' property) and returns an object where keys are categories and values are the count of items in that category. Use the function `countItemsByCategory(items)`.

Example: `countItemsByCategory([{name:'A',cat:'food'},{name:'B',cat:'tool'},{name:'C',cat:'food'}])` should return `{food:2, tool:1}`.
Example: `countItemsByCategory([{name:'D',cat:'drink'}])` should return `{drink:1}`.

title: Find Next Available Timeslot
spec:
Implement a function that finds the next available 30-minute timeslot, given a current time (Date object) and an array of occupied timeslots (each an object with 'start' and 'end' Date objects). It should return a Date object representing the start of the next free 30-minute slot. Use the function `findNextAvailableSlot(currentTime, occupiedSlots)`.

Example: `findNextAvailableSlot(new Date('2023-01-01T09:00:00'), [{start: new Date('2023-01-01T09:00:00'), end: new Date('2023-01-01T09:30:00')}])` should return `new Date('2023-01-01T09:30:00')`.
Example: `findNextAvailableSlot(new Date('2023-01-01T10:00:00'), [])` should return `new Date('2023-01-01T10:00:00')`.

title: Calculate Array Sum
spec:
Create a function that calculates the sum of all numbers in an array. The function should take an array of numbers and return a single number. Use the function `sumArray(numbers)`.

Example: `sumArray([1, 2, 3])` should return `6`.
Example: `sumArray([])` should return `0`.

title: Validate Hex Color Code
spec:
Implement a function that checks if a string is a valid 3-digit or 6-digit hexadecimal color code (e.g., '#FFF' or '#RRGGBB'). It must start with '#'. The function should take a string and return a boolean. Use the function `isValidHexColor(hexCode)`.

Example: `isValidHexColor('#ABC')` should return `true`.
Example: `isValidHexColor('#12345G')` should return `false`.

title: Remove Item from Inventory
spec:
Write a function that removes an item from an array of inventory objects based on its 'id'. The function should take the inventory array and an item ID (string or number) and return a new array with the item removed. Use the function `removeItemFromInventory(inventory, itemId)`.

Example: `removeItemFromInventory([{id:1, name:'A'}], 1)` should return `[]`.
Example: `removeItemFromInventory([{id:1, name:'A'}, {id:2, name:'B'}], 3)` should return `[{id:1, name:'A'}, {id:2, name:'B'}]`.

title: Get Events Within Time Range
spec:
Create a function that filters an array of event objects, returning only those that fall completely within a specified start and end time. Each event object has 'name', 'start' (Date), and 'end' (Date) properties. Use the function `getEventsInTimeRange(events, rangeStart, rangeEnd)`.

Example: `getEventsInTimeRange([{name:'A',start:new Date('2023-01-01T09:00'),end:new Date('2023-01-01T10:00')}], new Date('2023-01-01T08:00'), new Date('2023-01-01T11:00'))` should return `[{name:'A',start:...,end:...}]`.
Example: `getEventsInTimeRange([{name:'B',start:new Date('2023-01-01T09:00'),end:new Date('2023-01-01T10:00')}], new Date('2023-01-01T09:30'), new Date('2023-01-01T10:30'))` should return `[]`.

title: Check Tic-Tac-Toe Row Winner
spec:
Write a function that checks if there's a winner in any row of a 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe board. The board is represented as an array of three arrays (rows), with 'X', 'O', or null values. It returns 'X', 'O', or null. Use the function `checkTicTacToeRowWinner(board)`.

Example: `checkTicTacToeRowWinner([['X','X','X'],[null,'O',null],[null,null,'O']])` should return `'X'`.
Example: `checkTicTacToeRowWinner([['X','O','X'],['X','O',null],['O',null,'X']])` should return `null`.

title: Extract All Numbers from String
spec:
Create a function that extracts all numerical sequences from a given string and returns them as an array of numbers. Ignore non-numeric characters. Use the function `extractNumbers(text)`.

Example: `extractNumbers('The price is $10.99 for 2 items.')` should return `[10.99, 2]`.
Example: `extractNumbers('No numbers here.')` should return `[]`.

title: Get Object Keys
spec:
Write a function that returns an array of all enumerable string-keyed property names of an object. The function should take an object and return an array of strings. Use the function `getObjectKeys(obj)`.

Example: `getObjectKeys({a:1, b:2})` should return `['a', 'b']`.
Example: `getObjectKeys({})` should return `[]`.

title: Validate Simple Email Format
spec:
Implement a function that performs a basic validation of an email address string. It should check for the presence of '@' and '.' characters, and that '@' appears before '.'. It should return a boolean. Use the function `validateSimpleEmail(email)`.

Example: `validateSimpleEmail('test@example.com')` should return `true`.
Example: `validateSimpleEmail('testexample.com')` should return `false`.

title: Simulate Die Roll (Specific Sides)
spec:
Create a function that simulates rolling a die with a specified number of sides. It should take an integer `sides` (minimum 2) and return a random integer between 1 and `sides` (inclusive). Use the function `rollDie(sides)`.

Example: `rollDie(6)` might return `3` (any integer from 1-6).
Example: `rollDie(2)` might return `1` (any integer from 1-2).

title: Calculate Area of a Square
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the area of a square given the length of one of its sides. The function should accept a number (side length) and return a single number. Use the function `calculateSquareArea(side)`.

Example: `calculateSquareArea(5)` should return `25`.
Example: `calculateSquareArea(2.5)` should return `6.25`.

title: Add Item to Inventory
spec:
Write a function that adds a new item object to an array of inventory items. Each item object has 'id', 'name', and 'quantity' properties. The function should take the inventory array and a new item object, returning a new array with the item added. Use the function `addItemToInventory(inventory, newItem)`.

Example: `addItemToInventory([], {id:1, name:'A', quantity:10})` should return `[{id:1, name:'A', quantity:10}]`.
Example: `addItemToInventory([{id:1, name:'A', quantity:10}], {id:2, name:'B', quantity:5})` should return `[{id:1, name:'A', quantity:10}, {id:2, name:'B', quantity:5}]`.

title: Find Event by Name
spec:
Create a function that searches an array of event objects for an event with a specific name. Each event object has 'name', 'start', and 'end' properties. It should return the first matching event object or `null` if not found. Use the function `findEventByName(events, eventName)`.

Example: `findEventByName([{name:'Meeting'},{name:'Lunch'}], 'Lunch')` should return `{name:'Lunch'}`.
Example: `findEventByName([{name:'Meeting'}], 'Dinner')` should return `null`.

title: Calculate Product of Array
spec:
Write a function that calculates the product of all numbers in an array. The function should take an array of numbers and return a single number. Return 1 for an empty array. Use the function `productArray(numbers)`.

Example: `productArray([1, 2, 3])` should return `6`.
Example: `productArray([5, 0, 2])` should return `0`.

title: Convert Integer to Roman Numeral
spec:
Implement a function that converts an integer (between 1 and 3999) into its Roman numeral representation. The function should accept an integer and return a string. Use the function `integerToRoman(num)`.

Example: `integerToRoman(9)` should return `'IX'`.
Example: `integerToRoman(1994)` should return `'MCMXCIV'`.

title: Filter Objects by Property Value
spec:
Write a function that filters an array of objects based on a specific property's value. The function should take an array of objects, a property name (string), and a value. It returns a new array of objects matching that value. Use the function `filterByProperty(arr, prop, val)`.

Example: `filterByProperty([{id:1, type:'A'}, {id:2, type:'B'}], 'type', 'A')` should return `[{id:1, type:'A'}]`.
Example: `filterByProperty([{id:1, type:'A'}], 'id', 5)` should return `[]`.

title: Format Date to 'YYYY-MM-DD'
spec:
Create a function that formats a Date object into a 'YYYY-MM-DD' string. Ensure month and day are zero-padded if single digits. Use the function `formatDateToISO(date)`.

Example: `formatDateToISO(new Date('2023-01-05'))` should return `'2023-01-05'`.
Example: `formatDateToISO(new Date('2023-12-25'))` should return `'2023-12-25'`.

title: Simulate Queue Operation
spec:
Implement a function that simulates adding and removing elements from a queue. It takes an array representing the queue and a command string ('enqueue' or 'dequeue') with an optional item. It returns the updated queue array (for enqueue) or the dequeued item (for dequeue). Use the function `simulateQueue(queue, command, item)`.

Example: `simulateQueue([], 'enqueue', 'A')` should return `['A']`.
Example: `simulateQueue(['A', 'B'], 'dequeue')` should return `'A'` (and the queue would be `['B']`).

title: Check if Point is Inside Rectangle (2D)
spec:
Write a function that checks if a given point (object with x, y) is inside a rectangle. The rectangle is defined by its top-left corner (object with x, y), width, and height. Return a boolean. Use the function `isPointInRectangle(point, rectTopLeft, rectWidth, rectHeight)`.

Example: `isPointInRectangle({x:5,y:5}, {x:0,y:0}, 10, 10)` should return `true`.
Example: `isPointInRectangle({x:15,y:5}, {x:0,y:0}, 10, 10)` should return `false`.

title: Calculate Inventory Value
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the total monetary value of an inventory. The inventory is an array of item objects, each with 'quantity' (number) and 'unitPrice' (number). It should return a single number. Use the function `calculateInventoryValue(inventory)`.

Example: `calculateInventoryValue([{quantity:2, unitPrice:10}, {quantity:1, unitPrice:5}])` should return `25`.
Example: `calculateInventoryValue([])` should return `0`.

title: Calculate Time Difference in Minutes
spec:
Create a function that calculates the difference in minutes between two Date objects. The function should accept two Date objects and return an integer. Use the function `getTimeDifferenceInMinutes(date1, date2)`.

Example: `getTimeDifferenceInMinutes(new Date('2023-01-01T09:00:00'), new Date('2023-01-01T09:30:00'))` should return `30`.
Example: `getTimeDifferenceInMinutes(new Date('2023-01-01T10:00:00'), new Date('2023-01-01T09:00:00'))` should return `-60`.

title: Calculate Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD)
spec:
Write a function that calculates the Mean Absolute Deviation (MAD) of a dataset. The function should take an array of numbers and return a single number. MAD is the average of the absolute differences from the mean. Use the function `calculateMAD(data)`.

Example: `calculateMAD([1, 2, 3])` should return `0.666...`.
Example: `calculateMAD([10, 20, 30, 40])` should return `10`.

title: Get All Object Values
spec:
Implement a function that returns an array of all enumerable string-keyed property values of an object. The function should take an object and return an array. Use the function `getObjectValues(obj)`.

Example: `getObjectValues({a:1, b:2})` should return `[1, 2]`.
Example: `getObjectValues({})` should return `[]`.

title: Get Day of Week Name
spec:
Create a function that takes a Date object and returns the full name of the day of the week (e.g., 'Sunday', 'Monday'). Use the function `getDayOfWeekName(date)`.

Example: `getDayOfWeekName(new Date('2023-01-01'))` (a Sunday) should return `'Sunday'`.
Example: `getDayOfWeekName(new Date('2023-01-02'))` (a Monday) should return `'Monday'`.

title: Simulate Basic Counter
spec:
Write a function that simulates a simple counter. It takes an initial count and a command ('increment', 'decrement', 'reset'). It returns the updated count. Use the function `simulateCounter(currentCount, command)`.

Example: `simulateCounter(5, 'increment')` should return `6`.
Example: `simulateCounter(10, 'reset')` should return `0`.

title: Calculate Area of a Rhombus
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the area of a rhombus given the lengths of its two diagonals. The function should accept two numbers and return a single number. Use the formula: Area = (d1 * d2) / 2. Use the function `calculateRhombusArea(diagonal1, diagonal2)`.

Example: `calculateRhombusArea(6, 8)` should return `24`.
Example: `calculateRhombusArea(10, 5)` should return `25`.

title: Group Inventory by Supplier
spec:
Create a function that groups an array of inventory items by their 'supplier' property. It returns an object where keys are supplier names and values are arrays of items from that supplier. Use the function `groupInventoryBySupplier(inventory)`.

Example: `groupInventoryBySupplier([{name:'A',sup:'X'},{name:'B',sup:'Y'},{name:'C',sup:'X'}])` should return `{X:[{name:'A',sup:'X'},{name:'C',sup:'X'}], Y:[{name:'B',sup:'Y'}]}`.
Example: `groupInventoryBySupplier([])` should return `{}`.

title: Sort Events by Start Date
spec:
Write a function that sorts an array of event objects by their 'start' Date property in ascending order. Each event object has 'name', 'start' (Date), and 'end' (Date) properties. It should return a new sorted array. Use the function `sortEventsByStartDate(events)`.

Example: `sortEventsByStartDate([{name:'B',start:new Date('2023-01-02')},{name:'A',start:new Date('2023-01-01')}])` should return `[{name:'A',start:...},{name:'B',start:...}]`.
Example: `sortEventsByStartDate([])` should return `[]`.

title: Calculate Standard Deviation (Population)
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the population standard deviation of an array of numbers. It takes an array of numbers and returns a single number. Use the function `calculatePopulationStdDev(data)`.

Example: `calculatePopulationStdDev([1, 2, 3])` should return approximately `0.816`.
Example: `calculatePopulationStdDev([5, 5, 5])` should return `0`.

title: Factorial Calculation (Iterative)
spec:
Implement an iterative function to calculate the factorial of a non-negative integer. The function should accept an integer 'n' and return its factorial. Use the function `iterativeFactorial(n)`.

Example: `iterativeFactorial(5)` should return `120`.
Example: `iterativeFactorial(0)` should return `1`.

title: Format Date to 'DD/MM/YY'
spec:
Write a function that formats a Date object into a 'DD/MM/YY' string. Ensure month and day are zero-padded, and the year is two digits. Use the function `formatDateShort(date)`.

Example: `formatDateShort(new Date('2023-01-05'))` should return `'05/01/23'`.
Example: `formatDateShort(new Date('1999-12-31'))` should return `'31/12/99'`.

title: Simulate Random Hexadecimal String
spec:
Create a function that generates a random hexadecimal string of a specified length. The string should only contain valid hexadecimal characters (0-9, a-f). The function should accept an integer 'length' and return a string. Use the function `generateRandomHexString(length)`.

Example: `generateRandomHexString(4)` might return `'a3f0'`.
Example: `generateRandomHexString(8)` might return `'1b2c3d4e'`.

title: Calculate Area of a Parallelogram
spec:
Write a function that calculates the area of a parallelogram given its base and height. The function should accept two numbers and return a single number. Use the formula: Area = base * height. Use the function `calculateParallelogramArea(base, height)`.

Example: `calculateParallelogramArea(10, 5)` should return `50`.
Example: `calculateParallelogramArea(7.5, 4)` should return `30`.

title: Get Items by Tag
spec:
Implement a function that filters an array of item objects based on whether they contain a specific tag. Each item object has a 'tags' property, which is an array of strings. The function should return a new array of matching items. Use the function `getItemsByTag(items, tag)`.

Example: `getItemsByTag([{name:'A', tags:['red','big']},{name:'B', tags:['blue']}], 'red')` should return `[{name:'A', tags:['red','big']}]`.
Example: `getItemsByTag([{name:'C', tags:['green']}], 'yellow')` should return `[]`.

title: Check if Dates are on Same Day
spec:
Create a function that checks if two Date objects represent the same calendar day, ignoring time. The function should accept two Date objects and return a boolean. Use the function `isSameDay(date1, date2)`.

Example: `isSameDay(new Date('2023-01-01T10:00'), new Date('2023-01-01T15:00'))` should return `true`.
Example: `isSameDay(new Date('2023-01-01'), new Date('2023-01-02'))` should return `false`.

title: Text Processing: Reverse a String
spec: Implement a function that reverses a given string. The function should take one string as input and return the reversed string. Use the function name `reverseString`.

title: Arithmetic: Calculate Fibonacci Number
spec: Create a function to calculate the nth Fibonacci number. The function should take an integer `n` as input and return the nth Fibonacci number. Use the function name `fibonacci`.

title: Records: Get Object Keys (Sorted)
spec: Write a function that returns an array of an object's own enumerable property names, sorted alphabetically. The function should take an object as input and return an array of strings. Use the function name `getSortedKeys`.

title: Dates: Check if Date is in the Past
spec: Implement a function that checks if a given date is in the past relative to the current date. The function should take a `Date` object as input and return a boolean. Use the function name `isPastDate`.
example_calls: isPastDate(new Date('2023-01-01')); // Expected: true (if current date is after 2023-01-01)
isPastDate(new Date('2099-12-31')); // Expected: false (if current date is before 2099-12-31)

title: Simple Simulation: Coin Flip
spec: Implement a function that simulates a coin flip, returning either 'Heads' or 'Tails'. The function should take no input and return one of the two strings. Use the function name `coinFlip`.

title: Scheduling: Get Events Starting Today
spec: Implement a function that filters a list of event objects to return only those starting on the current day. Each event object has a `startDate` property (Date object). The function takes an array of event objects and returns an array of event objects. Use the function name `getTodaysEvents`.
example_calls: getTodaysEvents([{name: 'Meeting', startDate: new Date()}, {name: 'Party', startDate: new Date('2024-12-25')}]); // Expected: [{name: 'Meeting', startDate: new Date()}] (assuming today is the current date)
getTodaysEvents([{name: 'Party', startDate: new Date('2024-12-25')}]); // Expected: [] (assuming today is not 2024-12-25)

title: Games: Rock Paper Scissors Round
spec: Simulate a single round of Rock Paper Scissors. The function takes two strings, `player1Choice` and `player2Choice` ('rock', 'paper', or 'scissors'), and returns a string indicating the winner ('Player 1', 'Player 2', or 'Tie'). Use the function name `rockPaperScissors`.

title: Text Processing: Count Words in String
spec: Implement a function that counts the number of words in a given string. Words are separated by spaces. The function should take a string as input and return a number. Use the function name `countWords`.

title: Records: Find Object by Property Value
spec: Write a function to find the first object in an array that has a specific property value. The function takes an array of objects, a property name (string), and a value as input. It returns the matching object or `null`. Use the function name `findByProperty`.

title: Dates: Get Day of Week as Number
spec: Implement a function that returns the day of the week for a given date, where Sunday is 0, Monday is 1, and so on. The function should take a `Date` object as input and return a number (0-6). Use the function name `getDayOfWeekNumber`.

title: Parsing: Validate Simple HTML Tag
spec:
Create a function to validate if a string represents a simple, self-closing HTML tag (e.g., `
`, ``). It should check for `` format. The function takes a string and returns a boolean. Use the function name `isValidSelfClosingTag`.

title: Geometry: Calculate Perimeter of a Square
spec: Write a function that calculates the perimeter of a square given its side length. The function should take a number (side length) as input and return a number. Use the function name `squarePerimeter`.

title: Scheduling: Find Events by Title Keyword
spec: Implement a function that searches an array of event objects for events whose title contains a specific keyword (case-insensitive). Each event has a `title` property (string). The function takes an array of event objects and a keyword string, returning an array of matching event objects. Use the function name `findEventsByKeyword`.

title: Statistics: Calculate Average (Mean)
spec: Write a function to calculate the arithmetic mean (average) of an array of numbers. The function should take an array of numbers as input and return a single number. Use the function name `calculateAverage`.

title: Arithmetic: Calculate Product of Array
spec: Create a function to calculate the product of all numbers in an array. The function should take an array of numbers as input and return a single number. Use the function name `productArray`.

title: Records: Get Object Values (Sorted)
spec: Write a function that returns an array of an object's own enumerable property values, sorted based on their corresponding keys alphabetically. The function should take an object as input and return an array. Use the function name `getSortedValues`.

title: Simple Simulation: Generate Random Capital Letter
spec: Implement a function that generates a random uppercase English letter (A-Z). The function should take no input and return a single character string. Use the function name `randomCapitalLetter`.

title: Geometry: Check if Point is Inside Rectangle (2D)
spec: Write a function to check if a 2D point (px, py) is inside a rectangle defined by its top-left corner (rx, ry), width, and height. The function takes 6 numbers and returns a boolean. Use the function name `isPointInRectangle`.

title: Inventory: Get Total Value of Inventory
spec: Calculate the total monetary value of all items in an inventory. The function takes an inventory object (map of item names to quantities) and a prices object (map of item names to unit prices) as input. It returns a number representing the total value. Use the function name `calculateInventoryValue`.

title: Scheduling: Check if Two Events Overlap
spec: Implement a function that determines if two events, each with `startTime` and `endTime` (Date objects), overlap. The function takes two event objects as input and returns a boolean. Use the function name `doEventsOverlap`.
example_calls: doEventsOverlap({startTime: new Date('9:00'), endTime: new Date('10:00')}, {startTime: new Date('9:30'), endTime: new Date('10:30')}); // Expected: true
doEventsOverlap({startTime: new Date('9:00'), endTime: new Date('10:00')}, {startTime: new Date('10:00'), endTime: new Date('11:00')}); // Expected: false

title: Statistics: Calculate Variance (Population)
spec: Write a function to calculate the population variance of an array of numbers. The function should take an array of numbers as input and return a single number. Use the function name `calculatePopulationVariance`.

title: Text Processing: Remove Extra Spaces
spec: Implement a function that removes all leading, trailing, and duplicate internal spaces from a string. The function should take a string as input and return a string. Use the function name `removeExtraSpaces`.

title: Records: Filter Array of Objects by Property
spec: Write a function that filters an array of objects, keeping only those where a specified property matches a given value. The function takes an array of objects, a property name (string), and a value. It returns a new array of matching objects. Use the function name `filterObjectsByProperty`.

title: Dates: Get Number of Days in Month
spec: Implement a function that returns the number of days in a specific month and year. The function should take a year (number) and a 0-indexed month (0-11, number) as input, returning a number. Use the function name `getDaysInMonth`.
example_calls: getDaysInMonth(2024, 1); // Expected: 29 (February 2024 is a leap year)

title: Parsing: Basic CSV Row Parser
spec: Create a function that parses a single CSV row string into an array of strings. Assume values are comma-separated and do not contain commas themselves. The function takes a string and returns an array of strings. Use the function name `parseCsvRow`.

title: Simple Simulation: Generate Random String (Alphanumeric)
spec: Implement a function that generates a random alphanumeric string of a specified length. The function takes a number (length) as input and returns a string. Use the function name `generateRandomAlphanumeric`.

title: Geometry: Calculate Area of a Rectangle
spec: Write a function that calculates the area of a rectangle given its width and height. The function should take two numbers as input and return a number. Use the function name `rectangleArea`.

title: Inventory: Remove Item from Inventory
spec: Create a function to remove a specified quantity of an item from an inventory object. If the quantity to remove exceeds current stock, set stock to 0. If item doesn't exist, do nothing. The function takes an inventory object (map of item names to quantities), an item name (string), and a quantity (number). It modifies the inventory object in place. Use the function name `removeItemFromInventory`.
example_calls: let inv = {apple: 5, banana: 3}; removeItemFromInventory(inv, 'apple', 2); // inv should be {apple: 3, banana: 3}
let inv2 = {apple: 5}; removeItemFromInventory(inv2, 'apple', 10); // inv2 should be {apple: 0}

title: Scheduling: Find Available Slots (Simple)
spec: Implement a function that finds available time slots given a list of booked slots (each with `start` and `end` Date objects) and a desired duration. The function takes an array of booked slots, a start boundary (Date), an end boundary (Date), and a duration in minutes. It returns an array of available slot objects {start: Date, end: Date}. Use the function name `findAvailableSlots`.
example_calls: findAvailableSlots([{start: new Date('9:00'), end: new Date('10:00')}], new Date('8:00'), new Date('12:00'), 30); // Expected: [{start: new Date('8:00'), end: new Date('8:30')}, ..., {start: new Date('10:00'), end: new Date('10:30')}, ...]
findAvailableSlots([], new Date('9:00'), new Date('10:00'), 60); // Expected: [{start: new Date('9:00'), end: new Date('10:00')}]

title: Arithmetic: Check if Number is Palindrome
spec: Create a function that checks if a given number is a palindrome (reads the same forwards and backwards). The function should take an integer as input and return a boolean. Use the function name `isNumberPalindrome`.

title: Records: Get All Unique Values for a Key
spec: Write a function that extracts all unique values for a specified key from an array of objects. The function takes an array of objects and a key name (string). It returns an array of unique values. Use the function name `getUniqueValuesForKey`.

title: Dates: Format Date to 'DD-MM-YYYY'
spec: Implement a function that formats a `Date` object into a 'DD-MM-YYYY' string. The function should take a `Date` object as input and return a string. Use the function name `formatDateDDMMYYYY`.

title: Parsing: Extract Query Parameters from URL
spec: Create a function that extracts all query parameters from a URL string and returns them as an object. The function takes a URL string and returns an object where keys are parameter names and values are their decoded strings. Use the function name `getQueryParams`.

title: Geometry: Calculate Area of a Triangle (3 Points)
spec: Write a function to calculate the area of a triangle given the coordinates of its three vertices (x1, y1, x2, y2, x3, y3). Use the shoelace formula. The function takes 6 numbers and returns the area as a number. Use the function name `triangleAreaFromPoints`.

title: Inventory: Count Items by Category
spec: Count the total number of items for each category in a given inventory. The function takes an array of item objects, where each object has `name`, `category`, and `quantity` properties. It returns an object mapping category names to total quantities. Use the function name `countItemsByCategory`.
example_calls: countItemsByCategory([{name: 'A', category: 'Fruit', quantity: 5}, {name: 'B', category: 'Vegetable', quantity: 3}, {name: 'C', category: 'Fruit', quantity: 2}]); // Expected: {Fruit: 7, Vegetable: 3}

title: Scheduling: Sort Events by End Date
spec: Implement a function that sorts an array of event objects by their `endDate` property in ascending order. Each event object has `name`, `startDate`, and `endDate` (Date objects). The function takes an array of event objects and returns a new sorted array. Use the function name `sortEventsByEndDate`.
example_calls: sortEventsByEndDate([{name: 'B', endDate: new Date('2024-02-01')}, {name: 'A', endDate: new Date('2024-01-01')}]); // Expected: [{name: 'A', ...}, {name: 'B', ...}]

title: Games: Simulate Card Draw from Deck
spec: Simulate drawing a random card from a standard 52-card deck. The function takes no input and returns a string like 'Ace of Spades' or 'King of Hearts'. Use the function name `drawCard`.

title: Text Processing: Convert to Title Case
spec: Implement a function that converts a string to title case (first letter of each word capitalized). The function should take a string as input and return a string. Use the function name `toTitleCase`.
example_calls: toTitleCase('this is a test'); // Expected: 'This Is A Test'

title: Arithmetic: Calculate Least Common Multiple (LCM)
spec: Create a function to calculate the least common multiple (LCM) of two positive integers. The function should take two numbers as input and return a single number. Use the function name `calculateLCM`.

title: Records: Merge Two Objects (Shallow)
spec: Write a function that merges two objects into a new object. Properties from the second object should overwrite properties from the first if keys conflict. The function takes two objects and returns a new object. Use the function name `shallowMerge`.
example_calls: shallowMerge({a: 1, b: 2}, {b: 3, c: 4}); // Expected: {a: 1, b: 3, c: 4}

title: Dates: Calculate Difference in Hours
spec: Implement a function that calculates the difference between two `Date` objects in full hours. The function should take two `Date` objects (date1, date2) as input and return a number. Use the function name `diffInHours`.

title: Parsing: Validate US Zip Code
spec: Create a function that validates if a string is a valid 5-digit US zip code (e.g., '12345'). It should only contain digits. The function takes a string and returns a boolean. Use the function name `isValidUSZipCode`.

title: Arithmetic: Calculate Factorial (Recursive)
spec:
Write a recursive function to calculate the factorial of a non-negative integer. The input will be an integer between 0 and 10. Use `factorial(n)`.
Example: `factorial(5)` should return `120`. `factorial(0)` should return `1`.

title: Simple Simulation: Generate Random Integer
spec:
Implement a function that generates a random integer within a specified inclusive range. The range will be provided as `min` and `max`. Use `getRandomInt(min, max)`.
Example: `getRandomInt(1, 5)` should return a number like `3` (could be `1`, `2`, `4`, `5`). `getRandomInt(10, 10)` should return `10`.

title: Inventory: Increment Item Quantity
spec:
Write a function that takes an inventory array (objects with `id` and `quantity`) and an item `id` along with an `amount` to increment. Return the updated inventory. Use `incrementQuantity(inventory, id, amount)`.
Example: `incrementQuantity([{id:1,qty:5}], 1, 2)` should return `[{id:1,qty:7}]`. `incrementQuantity([{id:1,qty:5}], 2, 1)` should return `[{id:1,qty:5}]`.

title: Scheduling: Check if Date is a Weekend
spec:
Implement a function that determines if a given `Date` object falls on a weekend (Saturday or Sunday). Use `isWeekend(date)`.
Example: `isWeekend(new Date('2023-10-28'))` (Saturday) should return `true`. `isWeekend(new Date('2023-10-27'))` (Friday) should return `false`.

title: Games: Simulate Coin Toss Result
spec:
Implement a function that simulates a coin toss, returning either 'Heads' or 'Tails' randomly. Use `coinToss()`.
Example: `coinToss()` could return `'Heads'`. `coinToss()` could return `'Tails'`.

title: Arithmetic: Calculate Power (Exponentiation)
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the result of a base raised to an exponent. Do not use `Math.pow()`. Assume non-negative integer exponents. Use `calculatePower(base, exponent)`.
Example: `calculatePower(2, 3)` should return `8`. `calculatePower(5, 0)` should return `1`.

title: Parsing: Basic JSON String Validator
spec:
Write a function that attempts to parse a string as JSON and returns `true` if successful, `false` otherwise. Do not throw errors; handle them gracefully. Use `isValidJsonString(str)`.
Example: `isValidJsonString('{"name":"test"}')` should return `true`. `isValidJsonString('not json')` should return `false`.

title: Geometry: Calculate Hypotenuse
spec:
Create a function that calculates the hypotenuse of a right-angled triangle given the lengths of its two shorter sides. Use `calculateHypotenuse(a, b)`.
Example: `calculateHypotenuse(3, 4)` should return `5`. `calculateHypotenuse(5, 12)` should return `13`.

title: Inventory: List Items Below Quantity Threshold
spec:
Write a function that takes an inventory array (objects with `name` and `quantity`) and a `threshold` number. Return an array of item names whose quantity is below the threshold. Use `listItemsBelowThreshold(inventory, threshold)`.
Example: `listItemsBelowThreshold([{n:'A',q:5},{n:'B',q:2}], 3)` should return `['B']`. `listItemsBelowThreshold([{n:'A',q:5},{n:'B',q:2}], 1)` should return `[]`.

title: Scheduling: Group Events by Category
spec:
Implement a function that takes an array of event objects (each with `title` and `category`) and groups them into an object where keys are categories and values are arrays of event titles. Use `groupEventsByCategory(events)`.
Example: `groupEventsByCategory([{t:'A',c:'Work'},{t:'B',c:'Work'},{t:'C',c:'Personal'}])` should return `{Work: ['A', 'B'], Personal: ['C']}`. `groupEventsByCategory([])` should return `{}`.

title: Statistics: Calculate Sum of Squares
spec:
Create a function that calculates the sum of the squares of all numbers in an array. Use `sumOfSquares(numbers)`.
Example: `sumOfSquares([1, 2, 3])` should return `14` (1*1 + 2*2 + 3*3). `sumOfSquares([0, 1])` should return `1`.

title: Games: Check for Winner in Tic-Tac-Toe (Any Row)
spec:
Implement a function that checks if any row in a 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe board has a winner. The board is represented as a 2D array. Return the winning player's symbol ('X' or 'O') or `null`. Use `checkRowWinner(board)`.
Example: `checkRowWinner([['X','X','X'],['O','_','_'],['_','_','_']])` should return `'X'`. `checkRowWinner([['X','O','X'],['O','X','O'],['X','O','_']])` should return `null`.

title: Simple Simulation: Generate Random Element from Array
spec:
Implement a function that takes an array and returns a randomly selected element from it. Assume the array is non-empty. Use `getRandomElement(arr)`.
Example: `getRandomElement(['apple', 'banana', 'cherry'])` could return `'banana'`. `getRandomElement([1, 2])` could return `1` or `2`.

title: Inventory: Group Items by Supplier
spec:
Write a function that takes an array of item objects (each with `name` and `supplier`) and groups them into an object where keys are suppliers and values are arrays of item names. Use `groupItemsBySupplier(items)`.
Example: `groupItemsBySupplier([{n:'A',s:'X'},{n:'B',s:'Y'},{n:'C',s:'X'}])` should return `{X: ['A', 'C'], Y: ['B']}`. `groupItemsBySupplier([])` should return `{}`.

title: Scheduling: Find First Available Timeslot
spec:
Implement a function that finds the first available consecutive timeslot of a given `duration` (in minutes) within a `day` (Date object). Assume a workday from 9 AM to 5 PM (inclusive of 9 AM, exclusive of 5 PM). Takes an array of busy `intervals` (each `{start: Date, end: Date}`). Return the start `Date` of the available slot or `null`. Use `findFirstAvailableSlot(day, duration, busyIntervals)`.
Example: `findFirstAvailableSlot(new Date('2023-10-27T09:00:00'), 60, [])` should return `new Date('2023-10-27T09:00:00')`. `findFirstAvailableSlot(new Date('2023-10-27T09:00:00'), 60, [{start: new Date('2023-10-27T09:00:00'), end: new Date('2023-10-27T10:00:00')}])` should return `new Date('2023-10-27T10:00:00')`.

title: Games: Simulate Die Roll (Specific Sides)
spec:
Implement a function that simulates a die roll with a specified number of `sides`. Return an integer between 1 and `sides` (inclusive). Use `rollDie(sides)`.
Example: `rollDie(6)` could return `3`. `rollDie(20)` could return `15`.

title: Records: Transform Array of Objects to Map by Key
spec:
Create a function that takes an array of objects and a `key` string, returning a `Map` where keys are the values of the specified `key` from each object, and values are the objects themselves. If duplicate keys, the last one wins. Use `arrayToMapByKey(arr, key)`.
Example: `arrayToMapByKey([{id:1,n:'A'},{id:2,n:'B'}], 'id')` should return `Map {1 => {id:1,n:'A'}, 2 => {id:2,n:'B'}}`. `arrayToMapByKey([{id:1,n:'A'},{id:1,n:'C'}], 'id')` should return `Map {1 => {id:1,n:'C'}}`.

title: Dates: Check if Date is Today
spec:
Implement a function that determines if a given `Date` object represents the current day (ignoring time). Use `isToday(date)`.
Example: `isToday(new Date())` should return `true`. `isToday(new Date('2022-01-01'))` should return `false` (assuming today isn't Jan 1, 2022).

title: Parsing: Extract Hashtags from String
spec:
Write a function that extracts all hashtags (words starting with '#') from a given string and returns them as an array of strings (without the '#'). Hashtags consist only of alphanumeric characters. Use `extractHashtags(text)`.
Example: `extractHashtags('Hello #world, this is a #test.')` should return `['world', 'test']`. `extractHashtags('No hashtags here.')` should return `[]`.

title: Simple Simulation: Simulate HTTP Status Code
spec:
Implement a function that simulates returning a random common HTTP status code (e.g., 200, 400, 401, 403, 404, 500, 503). Use `simulateHttpStatus()`.
Example: `simulateHttpStatus()` could return `200`. `simulateHttpStatus()` could return `404`.

title: Geometry: Calculate Area of a Circle
spec:
Create a function that calculates the area of a circle given its radius. Use `Math.PI`. Use `calculateCircleArea(radius)`.
Example: `calculateCircleArea(1)` should return `3.141592653589793`. `calculateCircleArea(0)` should return `0`.

title: Scheduling: Filter Events by Date Range
spec:
Implement a function that filters an array of event objects (each with `startDate: Date`) to only include events falling within a specified `startDate` and `endDate` (inclusive). Use `filterEventsByDateRange(events, startDate, endDate)`.
Example: `filterEventsByDateRange([{s:new Date('2023-01-05')}], new Date('2023-01-01'), new Date('2023-01-10'))` should return `[{s:new Date('2023-01-05')}]`. `filterEventsByDateRange([{s:new Date('2023-01-15')}], new Date('2023-01-01'), new Date('2023-01-10'))` should return `[]`.

title: Statistics: Calculate Z-score
spec:
Create a function that calculates the Z-score for a given `value` within a dataset, requiring the `mean` and `standardDeviation` of the dataset. Use `calculateZScore(value, mean, standardDeviation)`.
Example: `calculateZScore(75, 70, 5)` should return `1`. `calculateZScore(60, 70, 5)` should return `-2`.

title: Games: Check for Winner in Tic-Tac-Toe (Any Column)
spec:
Implement a function that checks if any column in a 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe board has a winner. The board is represented as a 2D array. Return the winning player's symbol ('X' or 'O') or `null`. Use `checkColumnWinner(board)`.
Example: `checkColumnWinner([['X','O','_'],['X','_','O'],['X','_','_']])` should return `'X'`. `checkColumnWinner([['X','O','X'],['O','X','O'],['X','O','_']])` should return `null`.

title: Text Processing: Check if String is Anagram
spec:
Write a function that determines if two strings are anagrams of each other (contain the same characters with the same frequency, ignoring case and non-alphabetic characters). Use `areAnagrams(str1, str2)`.
Example: `areAnagrams('listen', 'silent')` should return `true`. `areAnagrams('hello', 'world')` should return `false`.

title: Arithmetic: Convert Decimal to Binary
spec:
Implement a function that converts a non-negative integer from decimal to its binary string representation. Use `decimalToBinary(decimalNum)`.
Example: `decimalToBinary(10)` should return `'1010'`. `decimalToBinary(0)` should return `'0'`.

title: Records: Merge Objects (Deep Merge)
spec:
Create a function that deeply merges two objects into a new object. Properties in the second object should override properties in the first. Nested objects should also be merged. Use `deepMerge(obj1, obj2)`.
Example: `deepMerge({a:1,b:{c:2}}, {b:{d:3}})` should return `{a:1,b:{c:2,d:3}}`. `deepMerge({a:1}, {a:2})` should return `{a:2}`.

title: Dates: Get First Day of Month
spec:
Implement a function that takes a `Date` object and returns a new `Date` object representing the first day of the month of the input date, with time set to 00:00:00.000. Use `getFirstDayOfMonth(date)`.
Example: `getFirstDayOfMonth(new Date('2023-10-15T10:30:00'))` should return `new Date('2023-10-01T00:00:00')`. `getFirstDayOfMonth(new Date('2024-02-20'))` should return `new Date('2024-02-01T00:00:00')`.

title: Parsing: Parse CSV Line
spec:
Write a function that parses a single CSV line string into an array of strings. Assume values are comma-separated and may be enclosed in double quotes (which should be removed). Quotes inside quoted fields are escaped by doubling them (e.g., '"A""B"' becomes 'A"B'). Use `parseCsvLine(line)`.
Example: `parseCsvLine('a,b,c')` should return `['a', 'b', 'c']`. `parseCsvLine('"hello,world","test"')` should return `['hello,world', 'test']`.

title: Simple Simulation: Generate Random Lorem Ipsum Sentence
spec:
Implement a function that generates a random short 'Lorem Ipsum' style sentence (3-7 words). Use a predefined list of simple words. Use `generateLoremIpsumSentence()`.
Example: `generateLoremIpsumSentence()` could return `'Lorem ipsum dolor sit amet.'`. `generateLoremIpsumSentence()` could return `'Consectetur adipiscing elit.'`.

title: Scheduling: Sort Events by Title Alphabetically
spec:
Implement a function that takes an array of event objects (each with `title: string`) and sorts them alphabetically by title. Return a new sorted array. Use `sortEventsByTitle(events)`.
Example: `sortEventsByTitle([{t:'B'},{t:'A'},{t:'C'}])` should return `[{t:'A'},{t:'B'},{t:'C'}]`. `sortEventsByTitle([])` should return `[]`.

title: Games: Check for Winner in Tic-Tac-Toe (Any Diagonal)
spec:
Implement a function that checks if any diagonal in a 3x3 Tic-Tac-Toe board has a winner. The board is represented as a 2D array. Return the winning player's symbol ('X' or 'O') or `null`. Use `checkDiagonalWinner(board)`.
Example: `checkDiagonalWinner([['X','O','_'],['_','X','O'],['_','_','X']])` should return `'X'`. `checkDiagonalWinner([['O','X','_'],['X','O','O'],['_','_','X']])` should return `'O'`.

title: Text Processing: Word Count
spec:
Write a function that counts the number of words in a given string. Words are separated by spaces and punctuation should not be counted as words. Use `wordCount(text)`.
Example: `wordCount('Hello world!')` should return `2`. `wordCount('  One   two three.  ')` should return `3`.

title: Arithmetic: Convert Binary to Decimal
spec:
Implement a function that converts a binary string representation to its decimal integer equivalent. Assume valid binary strings. Use `binaryToDecimal(binaryStr)`.
Example: `binaryToDecimal('1010')` should return `10`. `binaryToDecimal('1111')` should return `15`.

title: Records: Find Object by Property and Value (Case-Insensitive)
spec:
Create a function that searches an array of objects for an object where a specified `key`'s string value matches a `targetValue` (case-insensitive). Return the first matching object or `null`. Use `findObjectByCaseInsensitive(arr, key, targetValue)`.
Example: `findObjectByCaseInsensitive([{n:'Apple'},{n:'Banana'}], 'n', 'apple')` should return `{n:'Apple'}`. `findObjectByCaseInsensitive([{n:'Apple'}], 'n', 'orange')` should return `null`.

title: Parsing: Extract Domain from URL
spec:
Write a function that takes a URL string and extracts its domain name. Handle common protocols (http, https). The domain should not include 'www.' or protocol. Use `getDomainFromUrl(url)`.
Example: `getDomainFromUrl('https://www.example.com/path')` should return `'example.com'`. `getDomainFromUrl('http://sub.domain.org')` should return `'sub.domain.org'`. `getDomainFromUrl('ftp://unknown.net')` should return `null`.

title: Records: Deep Clone Object
spec:
Write a function to create a deep clone of a JavaScript object, handling nested objects and arrays. The function should be named `deepCloneObject`. It takes one object argument and returns a new object. Assume no circular references.
Example: `deepCloneObject({a: 1, b: {c: 2}})` should return `{a: 1, b: {c: 2}}` (a new object entirely). `deepCloneObject([1, {x: 2}])` should return `[1, {x: 2}]` (new array and object).

title: Scheduling: Find Events by Day of Week
spec:
Create a function that filters an array of event objects, returning only those events that occur on a specific day of the week (e.g., 'Monday'). Each event object has a `startDate` (Date object). The function should be named `findEventsByDayOfWeek`. It takes an array of event objects and a string representing the day of the week (e.g., 'Monday'), and returns an array of event objects.
Example: `findEventsByDayOfWeek([{startDate: new Date('2023-10-23')}, {startDate: new Date('2023-10-24')}], 'Monday')` should return `[{startDate: new Date('2023-10-23')}]` (2023-10-23 is a Monday). `findEventsByDayOfWeek([{startDate: new Date('2023-10-23')}], 'Tuesday')` should return `[]`.

title: Arithmetic: Calculate Greatest Common Divisor (GCD)
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the greatest common divisor (GCD) of two non-negative integers using the Euclidean algorithm. The function should be named `calculateGCD`. It takes two numbers (a, b) and returns a number.
Example: `calculateGCD(48, 18)` should return `6`. `calculateGCD(101, 103)` should return `1`.

title: Records: Count Occurrences of Key Value
spec:
Create a function that counts how many times a specific value appears for a given key across an array of objects. The function should be named `countKeyValueOccurrences`. It takes an array of objects, a string (key), and a value to search for, and returns a number.
Example: `countKeyValueOccurrences([{a: 1}, {a: 2}, {a: 1}], 'a', 1)` should return `2`. `countKeyValueOccurrences([{name: 'Alice'}, {name: 'Bob'}], 'name', 'Charlie')` should return `0`.

title: Geometry: Calculate Circumference of a Circle
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the circumference of a circle given its radius. Use `Math.PI` for pi. The function should be named `circumferenceOfCircle`. It takes one number argument (radius) and returns a number.
Example: `circumferenceOfCircle(1)` should return `6.2831...`. `circumferenceOfCircle(2.5)` should return `15.7079...`.

title: Inventory: Filter Items by Stock Level
spec:
Write a function that filters an array of inventory items, returning only those items whose quantity is above a specified minimum. Each item object has a `name` and `quantity`. The function should be named `filterByStockLevel`. It takes an array of item objects and a minimum quantity (number), and returns an array of item objects.
Example: `filterByStockLevel([{name: 'A', quantity: 5}, {name: 'B', quantity: 12}], 10)` should return `[{name: 'B', quantity: 12}]`. `filterByStockLevel([{name: 'C', quantity: 3}], 5)` should return `[]`.

title: Scheduling: Get Events Starting After Date
spec:
Create a function that filters an array of event objects, returning only those events that start strictly after a given date. Each event object has a `startDate` (Date object). The function should be named `getEventsStartingAfter`. It takes an array of event objects and a `Date` object, and returns an array of event objects.
Example: `getEventsStartingAfter([{startDate: new Date('2023-01-01')}, {startDate: new Date('2023-01-05')}], new Date('2023-01-03'))` should return `[{startDate: new Date('2023-01-05')}]`. `getEventsStartingAfter([{startDate: new Date('2023-01-01')}], new Date('2023-01-01'))` should return `[]`.

title: Arithmetic: Convert Roman Numeral to Integer
spec:
Implement a function that converts a Roman numeral string (e.g., 'IV', 'XI') into its corresponding integer value. Assume valid Roman numerals up to 3999. The function should be named `romanToInt`. It takes one string argument and returns a number.
Example: `romanToInt('IV')` should return `4`. `romanToInt('MCMXCIV')` should return `1994`.

title: Records: Rename Object Key
spec:
Write a function that takes an object, an old key name, and a new key name, and returns a new object with the key renamed. The original object should not be mutated. If the old key does not exist, the object should be returned as is. The function should be named `renameObjectKey`. It takes an object, an old key string, and a new key string, and returns an object.
Example: `renameObjectKey({name: 'Alice', age: 30}, 'name', 'fullName')` should return `{fullName: 'Alice', age: 30}`. `renameObjectKey({a: 1}, 'b', 'c')` should return `{a: 1}`.

title: Dates: Get Last Day of Month
spec:
Implement a function that takes a JavaScript `Date` object and returns a new `Date` object representing the last day of that month. The time component should be set to 00:00:00. The function should be named `getLastDayOfMonth`. It takes one `Date` object and returns a `Date` object.
Example: `getLastDayOfMonth(new Date(2023, 0, 15))` should return `new Date(2023, 0, 31)`. `getLastDayOfMonth(new Date(2024, 1, 10))` should return `new Date(2024, 1, 29)` (leap year).

title: Simple Simulation: Simulate Progress Bar
spec:
Create a function that simulates the state of a progress bar. It takes a current value and a total value and returns the progress as a percentage string (e.g., '50%'). Handle edge cases for zero total or current exceeding total. The function should be named `simulateProgressBar`. It takes two numbers (current, total) and returns a string.
Example: `simulateProgressBar(50, 100)` should return `'50%'`. `simulateProgressBar(10, 0)` should return `'0%'`. `simulateProgressBar(120, 100)` should return `'100%'`.

title: Inventory: Find Items by Name Keyword
spec:
Write a function that searches an array of inventory items for items whose names contain a specific keyword (case-insensitive). Each item object has a `name` and `quantity`. The function should be named `findItemsByNameKeyword`. It takes an array of item objects and a string (keyword), and returns an array of item objects.
Example: `findItemsByNameKeyword([{name: 'Apple', quantity: 10}, {name: 'Orange', quantity: 5}], 'app')` should return `[{name: 'Apple', quantity: 10}]`. `findItemsByNameKeyword([{name: 'Banana'}], 'fruit')` should return `[]`.

title: Scheduling: Check if Date is in Future
spec:
Create a function that determines if a given `Date` object represents a date in the future (after the current date and time). The function should be named `isDateInFuture`. It takes one `Date` object and returns a boolean.
Example: `isDateInFuture(new Date(new Date().getTime() + 60000))` (1 minute from now) should return `true`. `isDateInFuture(new Date(2000, 0, 1))` should return `false`.

title: Games: Calculate Dice Roll Sum
spec:
Create a function that simulates rolling multiple dice and returns their sum. It takes the number of dice and the number of sides per die. Each die roll should be random. The function should be named `rollDiceSum`. It takes two numbers (numDice, sidesPerDie) and returns a number.
Example: `rollDiceSum(2, 6)` could return `7` (e.g., 3 + 4). `rollDiceSum(1, 20)` could return `15`.

title: Text Processing: Remove HTML Tags
spec:
Write a function that takes a string containing HTML and removes all HTML tags, leaving only the plain text content. Assume well-formed, simple tags. The function should be named `removeHtmlTags`. It takes one string argument and returns a string. Example: `removeHtmlTags('

Hello world!

')` should return `'Hello world!'`. `removeHtmlTags('

Text

')` should return `'Text'`.

title: Records: Group Objects by Property
spec:
Create a function that takes an array of objects and a property name, and groups the objects into an object where keys are the unique values of that property. The function should be named `groupObjectsByProperty`. It takes an array of objects and a string (propertyName) and returns an object.
Example: `groupObjectsByProperty([{type: 'fruit', name: 'Apple'}, {type: 'veg', name: 'Carrot'}, {type: 'fruit', name: 'Banana'}], 'type')` should return `{fruit: [{type: 'fruit', name: 'Apple'}, {type: 'fruit', name: 'Banana'}], veg: [{type: 'veg', name: 'Carrot'}]}`. `groupObjectsByProperty([{id: 1}, {id: 2}], 'id')` should return `{1: [{id: 1}], 2: [{id: 2}]}`.

title: Parsing: Validate URL Structure
spec:
Write a function that performs a basic validation of a URL string. It should check for a valid protocol (http/https), a non-empty domain, and a period in the domain. It doesn't need to be a full RFC validator. The function should be named `isValidURL`. It takes one string argument and returns a boolean.
Example: `isValidURL('https://example.com/path')` should return `true`. `isValidURL('ftp://invalid')` should return `false`. `isValidURL('www.example.com')` should return `false`.

title: Geometry: Calculate Volume of a Cube
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the volume of a cube given its side length. The function should be named `volumeOfCube`. It takes one number argument (sideLength) and returns a number.
Example: `volumeOfCube(2)` should return `8`. `volumeOfCube(3.5)` should return `42.875`.

title: Inventory: Deduct Item Quantity
spec:
Write a function to deduct a specified amount from an item's quantity in an array of inventory objects. Each item has an `id` and `quantity`. If the deduction would make the quantity negative, it should be set to 0. The function should return a new array. The function should be named `deductItemQuantity`. It takes an array of item objects, an item `id` (number), and a `deductionAmount` (number), and returns an array of item objects.
Example: `deductItemQuantity([{id: 1, quantity: 10}], 1, 3)` should return `[{id: 1, quantity: 7}]`. `deductItemQuantity([{id: 2, quantity: 5}], 2, 8)` should return `[{id: 2, quantity: 0}]`.

title: Scheduling: Get Upcoming Events (N Days)
spec:
Create a function that filters an array of event objects, returning only those events that start within the next `n` days from the current date. Each event object has a `startDate` (Date object). The function should be named `getUpcomingEvents`. It takes an array of event objects and a number (numDays), and returns an array of event objects.
Example: `getUpcomingEvents([{startDate: new Date('2023-10-25')}, {startDate: new Date('2023-11-01')}], 7)` (assuming today is Oct 24, 2023) should return `[{startDate: new Date('2023-10-25')}]`. `getUpcomingEvents([{startDate: new Date('2023-10-25')}], 0)` (assuming today is Oct 24, 2023) should return `[]`.

title: Statistics: Calculate Quartiles
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the first (Q1) and third (Q3) quartiles of a given array of numbers. Return an object with `q1` and `q3` properties. Assume the array is sorted before calculation. The function should be named `calculateQuartiles`. It takes an array of numbers and returns an object `{q1: number, q3: number}`.
Example: `calculateQuartiles([1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7])` should return `{q1: 2, q3: 6}`. `calculateQuartiles([1, 2, 3, 4])` should return `{q1: 1.5, q3: 3.5}`.

title: Text Processing: Count Words in Sentence
spec:
Create a function that counts the number of words in a given sentence string. Words are separated by spaces. Punctuation attached to words should be considered part of the word for counting purposes. The function should be named `countWordsInSentence`. It takes one string argument and returns a number.
Example: `countWordsInSentence('Hello world, this is a test!')` should return `6`. `countWordsInSentence(' One  two   three ')` should return `3`.

title: Records: Find Objects with Missing Key
spec:
Write a function that filters an array of objects, returning only those objects that do not have a specified key. The function should be named `findObjectsWithMissingKey`. It takes an array of objects and a string (keyName) and returns an array of objects.
Example: `findObjectsWithMissingKey([{a: 1}, {b: 2}], 'a')` should return `[{b: 2}]`. `findObjectsWithMissingKey([{a: 1, b: 2}], 'c')` should return `[{a: 1, b: 2}]`.

title: Dates: Format Time to 'HH:MM AM/PM'
spec:
Implement a function that takes a JavaScript `Date` object and formats its time component into a string in 'HH:MM AM/PM' format. Ensure single-digit hours/minutes are padded with a leading zero. The function should be named `formatTimeAMPM`. It takes one `Date` object and returns a string.
Example: `formatTimeAMPM(new Date(2023, 0, 1, 14, 30))` should return `'02:30 PM'`. `formatTimeAMPM(new Date(2023, 0, 1, 9, 5))` should return `'09:05 AM'`.

title: Simple Simulation: Generate Random Item from Weighted List
spec:
Create a function that selects a random item from a list, where each item has an associated weight. Items with higher weights should have a higher chance of being selected. The function should be named `getRandomWeightedItem`. It takes an array of objects `{item: any, weight: number}` and returns the `item` property of a randomly selected object.
Example: `getRandomWeightedItem([{item: 'A', weight: 1}, {item: 'B', weight: 9}])` is likely to return `'B'`. `getRandomWeightedItem([{item: 'C', weight: 5}])` should return `'C'`.

title: Geometry: Calculate Area of a Trapezoid
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the area of a trapezoid given its two parallel bases and its height. The function should be named `areaOfTrapezoid`. It takes three numbers (base1, base2, height) and returns a number.
Example: `areaOfTrapezoid(2, 4, 3)` should return `9` ((2+4)/2 * 3). `areaOfTrapezoid(5, 5, 10)` should return `50`.

title: Inventory: Get Items by Date Added (Range)
spec:
Write a function that filters an array of inventory items, returning only those items added within a specific date range (inclusive). Each item object has a `name` and `dateAdded` (Date object). The function should be named `getItemsByDateAddedRange`. It takes an array of item objects, a `startDate` (Date object), and an `endDate` (Date object), and returns an array of item objects.
Example: `getItemsByDateAddedRange([{name: 'A', dateAdded: new Date('2023-01-05')}, {name: 'B', dateAdded: new Date('2023-01-10')}], new Date('2023-01-01'), new Date('2023-01-07'))` should return `[{name: 'A', dateAdded: new Date('2023-01-05')}]`. `getItemsByDateAddedRange([{name: 'C', dateAdded: new Date('2023-02-15')}], new Date('2023-03-01'), new Date('2023-03-31'))` should return `[]`.

title: Scheduling: Find First Available Time Slot (Gaps)
spec:
Create a function that finds the first available time slot of a specified duration within a given daily schedule. The schedule is an array of `{start: Date, end: Date}` objects. Return the `start` date of the first suitable slot, or `null` if none found. Assume events are sorted. The function should be named `findFirstAvailableSlot`. It takes an array of event objects, a `Date` representing the start of the day to check, and a duration in minutes, and returns a `Date` object or `null`.
Example: `findFirstAvailableSlot([{start: new Date('2023-10-26T09:00:00'), end: new Date('2023-10-26T10:00:00')}], new Date('2023-10-26T08:00:00'), 60)` should return `new Date('2023-10-26T08:00:00')`. `findFirstAvailableSlot([{start: new Date('2023-10-26T09:00:00'), end: new Date('2023-10-26T10:00:00')}], new Date('2023-10-26T09:30:00'), 30)` should return `new Date('2023-10-26T10:00:00')`.

title: Statistics: Calculate Coefficient of Variation
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the Coefficient of Variation (CV) for an array of numbers. CV is the ratio of the standard deviation to the mean, expressed as a percentage. Handle cases where the mean is zero. The function should be named `calculateCoefficientOfVariation`. It takes an array of numbers and returns a number (percentage, e.g., 0.25 for 25%).
Example: `calculateCoefficientOfVariation([10, 12, 10, 11, 13])` (mean=11, stdDev=1.14) should return approximately `0.103`. `calculateCoefficientOfVariation([5, 5, 5])` should return `0`.

title: Games: Check for Winner in Connect Four (Horizontal)
spec:
Write a function to check for a horizontal winner in a Connect Four board. The board is represented as a 2D array of strings ('R', 'Y', or ' '). A winner requires 4 consecutive identical pieces horizontally. The function should be named `checkConnectFourHorizontalWinner`. It takes a 2D array (board) and returns a string ('R', 'Y', or '') indicating the winner or no winner. Assume a 6x7 board input.
Example: `checkConnectFourHorizontalWinner([[' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' '],[' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' '],[' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' '],[' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' '],[' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' '],['R','R','R','R','Y','Y',' ']])` should return `'R'`. `checkConnectFourHorizontalWinner([[' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' ',' '],['R','R','Y','R',' ',' ',' ']])` should return `''`.

title: Text Processing: Slugify String
spec:
Create a function that converts a string into a URL-friendly slug. This involves converting to lowercase, replacing spaces with hyphens, and removing non-alphanumeric characters (except hyphens). The function should be named `slugify`. It takes one string argument and returns a string.
Example: `slugify('Hello World! This is a test.')` should return `'hello-world-this-is-a-test'`. `slugify('Product Name (123)')` should return `'product-name-123'`.

title: Records: Select Specific Keys from Object
spec:
Write a function that takes an object and an array of keys, and returns a new object containing only the specified keys and their values. Keys not present in the original object should be ignored. The function should be named `selectObjectKeys`. It takes an object and an array of strings (keysToSelect) and returns an object.
Example: `selectObjectKeys({a: 1, b: 2, c: 3}, ['a', 'c'])` should return `{a: 1, c: 3}`. `selectObjectKeys({x: 10}, ['y'])` should return `{}`.

title: Dates: Add/Subtract Days from Date
spec:
Implement a function that takes a JavaScript `Date` object and a number of days (positive to add, negative to subtract), and returns a new `Date` object with the adjusted date. The original date should not be mutated. The function should be named `addDaysToDate`. It takes one `Date` object and one number (days) and returns a `Date` object.
Example: `addDaysToDate(new Date('2023-01-01'), 5)` should return `new Date('2023-01-06')`. `addDaysToDate(new Date('2023-01-05'), -2)` should return `new Date('2023-01-03')`.

title: Parsing: Parse URL Query String
spec:
Write a function that parses a URL query string (e.g., '?name=Alice&age=30') into an object of key-value pairs. Handle multiple occurrences of the same key by storing values in an array. The function should be named `parseQueryString`. It takes one string argument and returns an object.
Example: `parseQueryString('?name=Alice&age=30')` should return `{name: 'Alice', age: '30'}`. `parseQueryString('?item=apple&item=banana')` should return `{item: ['apple', 'banana']}`.

title: Convert Base 10 to Any Base
spec:
Write a function to convert a base 10 integer to a string representation in a specified base (up to base 36). The function should handle positive integers. Define a function `convertToBase(decimal, base)` that takes an integer and a base, returning a string. 
Example 1: `convertToBase(10, 2)` should return `'1010'`. 
Example 2: `convertToBase(255, 16)` should return `'FF'`.

title: Deep Compare Two Objects
spec:
Create a function that performs a deep comparison between two objects to determine if they are structurally identical. This means comparing properties recursively, including nested objects and arrays. Define a function `deepCompare(obj1, obj2)` that returns a boolean. 
Example 1: `deepCompare({a: 1, b: {c: 2}}, {a: 1, b: {c: 2}})` should return `true`. 
Example 2: `deepCompare({a: 1, b: {c: 2}}, {a: 1, b: {c: 3}})` should return `false`.

title: Get Days Until Next Birthday
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the number of days remaining until a given birthday in the current or next year. The birthday should be provided as a `MM-DD` string. Define a function `getDaysUntilBirthday(birthdayString)` that returns an integer. 
Example 1: `getDaysUntilBirthday('12-25')` (if today is 12-24 of the same year) should return `1`. 
Example 2: `getDaysUntilBirthday('01-01')` (if today is 12-31 of the previous year) should return `1`.

title: Simulate Dice Roll Sum (Multiple Dice)
spec:
Create a function that simulates rolling multiple dice and returns their sum. The number of dice and the number of sides per die should be configurable. Define a function `rollDiceSum(numDice, sides)` that returns an integer. 
Example 1: `rollDiceSum(2, 6)` could return `7` (two 6-sided dice). 
Example 2: `rollDiceSum(3, 4)` could return `9` (three 4-sided dice).

title: Calculate Euclidean Distance (2D)
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the Euclidean distance between two points in a 2D plane. Each point will be an object with `x` and `y` properties. Define a function `euclideanDistance(p1, p2)` that returns a number. 
Example 1: `euclideanDistance({x: 0, y: 0}, {x: 3, y: 4})` should return `5`. 
Example 2: `euclideanDistance({x: 1, y: 1}, {x: 1, y: 5})` should return `4`.

title: Add Item to Inventory (with Quantity)
spec:
Write a function to add a new item to an inventory represented as an array of objects. If the item already exists (by name), update its quantity; otherwise, add it as a new entry. Define a function `addToInventory(inventory, itemName, quantity)` that modifies the `inventory` array and returns it. 
Example 1: `addToInventory([{name: 'apple', qty: 5}], 'banana', 10)` should return `[{name: 'apple', qty: 5}, {name: 'banana', qty: 10}]`. 
Example 2: `addToInventory([{name: 'apple', qty: 5}], 'apple', 3)` should return `[{name: 'apple', qty: 8}]`.

title: Schedule Task at Specific Time
spec:
Implement a function that schedules a callback function to run at a specific time of day (HH:MM format). It should return a `setTimeout` ID that can be cleared. Assume the scheduled time is for the *next* occurrence. Define a function `scheduleTask(timeString, callback)` that returns a timer ID. 
Example 1: `scheduleTask('23:59', () => console.log('Midnight approaching!'))` might set a timeout for a few minutes if current time is 23:55. 
Example 2: `scheduleTask('08:00', () => console.log('Good morning!'))`.

title: Calculate Median of Numbers
spec:
Create a function that calculates the median of a given array of numbers. The array might not be sorted. Handle both even and odd length arrays. Define a function `calculateMedian(numbers)` that returns a number. 
Example 1: `calculateMedian([1, 3, 2])` should return `2`. 
Example 2: `calculateMedian([1, 2, 3, 4])` should return `2.5`.

title: Check if String is Palindrome (Case-Insensitive)
spec:
Implement a function that checks if a given string is a palindrome, ignoring case and non-alphanumeric characters. Define a function `isPalindrome(str)` that returns a boolean. 
Example 1: `isPalindrome('RaceCar')` should return `true`. 
Example 2: `isPalindrome('Hello, world!')` should return `false`.

title: Group Objects by Multiple Properties
spec:
Create a function that groups an array of objects by one or more specified properties. The result should be an object where keys are the combined property values and values are arrays of matching objects. Define a function `groupByProperties(arr, keys)` that returns an object. 
Example 1: `groupByProperties([{a:1,b:2},{a:1,b:3}], ['a'])` should return `{ '1': [{a:1,b:2},{a:1,b:3}] }`. 
Example 2: `groupByProperties([{a:1,b:2},{a:1,b:3}], ['a', 'b'])` should return `{ '1-2': [{a:1,b:2}], '1-3': [{a:1,b:3}] }`.

title: Calculate Age from Date of Birth
spec:
Implement a function that calculates a person's current age given their date of birth. The date of birth should be a `Date` object. Define a function `calculateAge(dob)` that returns an integer. 
Example 1: `calculateAge(new Date('1990-05-15'))` (if today is 2023-05-14) should return `32`. 
Example 2: `calculateAge(new Date('1990-05-15'))` (if today is 2023-05-15) should return `33`.

title: Simulate Card Shuffle (Fisher-Yates)
spec:
Implement the Fisher-Yates (Knuth) shuffle algorithm to randomly reorder an array representing a deck of cards. The function should modify the array in place. Define a function `shuffleDeck(deck)` that takes an array and returns the shuffled array. 
Example 1: `shuffleDeck([1, 2, 3, 4])` could return `[3, 1, 4, 2]`. 
Example 2: `shuffleDeck(['A', 'K', 'Q'])` could return `['Q', 'A', 'K']`.

title: Find Next Available Appointment Slot
spec:
Given an array of booked appointment slots (e.g., `{start: Date, end: Date}`) and a desired duration, find the earliest available start time for a new appointment. Assume sorted existing appointments. Define a function `findNextAvailableSlot(bookedSlots, durationMinutes)` that returns a `Date` object or `null`. 
Example 1: `findNextAvailableSlot([{start: new Date('2023-10-26T10:00:00Z'), end: new Date('2023-10-26T11:00:00Z')}], 30)` (if current time allows) could return `new Date('2023-10-26T11:00:00Z')`. 
Example 2: `findNextAvailableSlot([{start: new Date('2023-10-26T09:00:00Z'), end: new Date('2023-10-26T09:30:00Z')}, {start: new Date('2023-10-26T10:00:00Z'), end: new Date('2023-10-26T10:30:00Z')}], 15)` could return `new Date('2023-10-26T09:30:00Z')`.

title: Calculate Mode of Numbers
spec:
Create a function that calculates the mode (the number that appears most often) of a given array of numbers. If there are multiple modes, return an array of them. Define a function `calculateMode(numbers)` that returns a number or an array of numbers. 
Example 1: `calculateMode([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 3])` should return `3`. 
Example 2: `calculateMode([1, 2, 2, 3, 3, 4])` should return `[2, 3]`.

title: Sentence Case Conversion
spec:
Write a function that converts a string to sentence case: the first letter of the first word is capitalized, and the rest are lowercase, preserving existing punctuation. Define a function `toSentenceCase(str)` that returns a string. 
Example 1: `toSentenceCase('hello world. this is a test.')` should return `'Hello world. This is a test.'`. 
Example 2: `toSentenceCase('a short sentence.')` should return `'A short sentence.'`.

title: Convert Base N to Base M
spec:
Implement a function to convert a number represented as a string in one base to a string representation in another base. The input base and output base can be between 2 and 36. Define a function `convertBase(numStr, fromBase, toBase)` that returns a string. 
Example 1: `convertBase('101', 2, 10)` should return `'5'`. 
Example 2: `convertBase('FF', 16, 10)` should return `'255'`.

title: Filter Object by Key List
spec:
Create a function that takes an object and an array of keys, returning a new object containing only the specified keys and their corresponding values. Define a function `filterObjectByKeys(obj, keys)` that returns an object. 
Example 1: `filterObjectByKeys({a:1, b:2, c:3}, ['a', 'c'])` should return `{a:1, c:3}`. 
Example 2: `filterObjectByKeys({x:10, y:20}, ['z'])` should return `{}`.

title: Get Quarter of the Year
spec:
Implement a function that returns the quarter of the year (1-4) for a given `Date` object. Define a function `getQuarter(date)` that returns an integer. 
Example 1: `getQuarter(new Date('2023-01-15'))` should return `1`. 
Example 2: `getQuarter(new Date('2023-07-20'))` should return `3`.

title: Calculate Angle Between Two Vectors (2D)
spec:
Implement a function that calculates the angle (in radians) between two 2D vectors. Each vector will be an array `[x, y]`. Define a function `angleBetweenVectors(v1, v2)` that returns a number. 
Example 1: `angleBetweenVectors([1, 0], [0, 1])` should return `Math.PI / 2` (90 degrees). 
Example 2: `angleBetweenVectors([1, 0], [-1, 0])` should return `Math.PI` (180 degrees).

title: Update Inventory Item Price
spec:
Write a function to update the price of a specific item in an inventory array of objects. If the item doesn't exist, it should not modify the inventory. Define a function `updateItemPrice(inventory, itemName, newPrice)` that modifies the `inventory` array and returns it. 
Example 1: `updateItemPrice([{name: 'apple', price: 1.0}], 'apple', 1.5)` should return `[{name: 'apple', price: 1.5}]`. 
Example 2: `updateItemPrice([{name: 'apple', price: 1.0}], 'banana', 2.0)` should return `[{name: 'apple', price: 1.0}]`.

title: Check Availability of Resources
spec:
Given a list of resources with their availability (`{id: 'A', available: true}`) and a list of requests for resources (`['A', 'C']`), determine which requests can be fulfilled. Return an array of resource IDs that are available and requested. Define a function `checkResourceAvailability(resources, requests)` that returns an array of strings. 
Example 1: `checkResourceAvailability([{id:'A',available:true},{id:'B',available:false}], ['A','C'])` should return `['A']`. 
Example 2: `checkResourceAvailability([{id:'X',available:false}], ['X'])` should return `[]`.

title: Remove Duplicates from Array (Case-Insensitive Strings)
spec:
Implement a function that removes duplicate strings from an array, treating case-insensitively. The order of the first occurrence should be preserved. Define a function `removeCaseInsensitiveDuplicates(arr)` that returns a new array. 
Example 1: `removeCaseInsensitiveDuplicates(['Apple', 'apple', 'Banana'])` should return `['Apple', 'Banana']`. 
Example 2: `removeCaseInsensitiveDuplicates(['a', 'B', 'A'])` should return `['a', 'B']`.

title: Convert Roman Numeral to Integer
spec:
Write a function that converts a Roman numeral string (e.g., 'IX', 'MCMXCIV') into its integer equivalent. Assume valid Roman numeral input. Define a function `romanToInt(roman)` that returns an integer. 
Example 1: `romanToInt('III')` should return `3`. 
Example 2: `romanToInt('LVIII')` should return `58`.

title: Get Keys with Specific Value
spec:
Create a function that takes an object and a target value, returning an array of all keys whose corresponding values match the target value. Define a function `getKeysByValue(obj, targetValue)` that returns an array of strings. 
Example 1: `getKeysByValue({a:1, b:2, c:1}, 1)` should return `['a', 'c']`. 
Example 2: `getKeysByValue({x:'hello', y:'world'}, 'test')` should return `[]`.

title: Get Week Number of Year
spec:
Implement a function that returns the week number (1-52 or 53) for a given `Date` object, according to ISO 8601 (week starts on Monday, first week has at least 4 days in new year). Define a function `getWeekNumber(date)` that returns an integer. 
Example 1: `getWeekNumber(new Date('2023-01-01'))` should return `52` (for 2022-12-26 to 2023-01-01). 
Example 2: `getWeekNumber(new Date('2023-01-09'))` should return `2`.

title: Parse Basic CSS Selector (Tag or Class)
spec:
Write a function that parses a simple CSS selector string (e.g., 'div', '.my-class') and extracts its type ('tag' or 'class') and value. Return an object `{type: '...', value: '...'}`. Handle only single tag names or single class names. Define a function `parseCssSelector(selector)` that returns an object. 
Example 1: `parseCssSelector('div')` should return `{ type: 'tag', value: 'div' }`. 
Example 2: `parseCssSelector('.header')` should return `{ type: 'class', value: 'header' }`.

title: Simulate Text Typing Effect
spec:
Create a function that simulates typing a string character by character into a DOM element with a delay between each character. It should return a Promise that resolves when typing is complete. Define an async function `simulateTyping(elementId, text, delayMs)` that returns a Promise. 
Example 1: `await simulateTyping('myDiv', 'Hello world!', 100)` would type 'Hello world!' into the div over time. 
Example 2: `await simulateTyping('statusP', 'Loading...', 50)`.

title: Calculate Area of an Ellipse
spec:
Write a function that calculates the area of an ellipse given the lengths of its semi-major and semi-minor axes. Use `Math.PI`. Define a function `calculateEllipseArea(semiMajorAxis, semiMinorAxis)` that returns a number. 
Example 1: `calculateEllipseArea(5, 3)` should return approximately `47.12`. 
Example 2: `calculateEllipseArea(2, 2)` should return approximately `12.56` (area of a circle).

title: Mark Inventory Item as Out of Stock
spec:
Implement a function that finds an item in an inventory array by name and sets its `inStock` property to `false`. If the item is not found, do nothing. Define a function `markOutOfStock(inventory, itemName)` that modifies the `inventory` array and returns it.
